subject: Clarify: conditional geolock / erasure timeline & backup carveouts
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@finovahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Finova Legal <contracts@finovahealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom@healthtech-partner.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA redline: geolock and backup erasure window

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — Finova's security team reviewed Redwood's DPA draft and we have a few follow-ups around the residency + deletion language before we can move to counter-signature:

1) Conditional geolock: you describe a "geofence" fallback where backups may be replicated for disaster recovery. We need explicit limits on which regions are allowed to receive backups and whether Finova must be notified before cross-border replication occurs.

2) Erasure timeline: our audit requires customer-data erasure "completed" within 30 days of an erase request, including copies in backups. Redwood's proposed language uses "reasonable commercial efforts" and a 90-day window for backup expiry. Can you clarify operationally how you will meet a 30-day certification?

3) Evidence: we'll need an evidence matrix for erasure events (logs, wipe certs, timestamps). Is there a standard template you provide?

Appreciate clear, actionable responses so our legal and infosec teams can sign off. Tom (our implementation partner) is CC'd since he may need to coordinate the DR carveout.

Best,
Olivia
Olivia Grant
Director, Security & Privacy
Finova Health

---
Attachments: none

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@finovahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA redline: geolock and backup erasure window

Olivia — thanks for the detailed note. Below are clear answers and next steps; attaching our proposed redline and an evidence matrix template for your review.

1) Conditional geolock / backup replication: Redwood will only replicate backups to regions explicitly listed in Schedule 2 (Operational Regions). For Finova we propose to enumerate the allowed EU regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1). Any cross-border replication outside that list requires advance written notice & approval from Finova (email to your contracts alias is fine).

2) Erasure timeline: operationally, our primary erase process will remove live customer data within 7 days. For backups we do a tombstone + scheduled retention pass. To meet the 30-day certification requirement we can offer the following commitment:
   - Live data: purged within 7 days of request.
   - Snapshot/backups (point-in-time): marked for expedited deletion and excluded from restore within 3 days; fully purged from active backup tiers within 30 days.
   - Cold/archival snapshots (if retained longer for compliance): will be flagged with Finova-specific carveouts and excluded unless explicitly agreed.

This is operationally supported by our backup system's expedited-retention workflow. We'll include a clause that Finova can request an "expedited eradication" run (one-time per erase request) to accelerate the purge and require Redwood to provide timestamped purge logs.

3) Evidence matrix: attaching our standard erase_evidence_matrix.xlsx. It includes log types, retention timestamps, cert templates, and a suggested audit-run cadence. If you prefer a custom format, point us to the fields you need and we'll adapt.

Next steps: Marcus, can you confirm the retention tiers and purge job SLAs for EU-managed backups? Karthik, happy to loop in Product/Infra if Finova asks for a BYOK or on-prem alternative.

Thanks,
Neha
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_proposed_redline.docx, erase_evidence_matrix.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@finovahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA redline: geolock and backup erasure window

Quick technical confirmation from infra:

- Retention tiers in EU: active (hot) backups kept for standard retention window, cold snapshots kept separately. For Finova we can configure the backup lifecycle so that snapshots created after the erase request are not restorable to the Finova tenant.
- Expedited purge: our compaction/garbage-collection job can be triggered to accelerate tombstone propagation; typical propagation to all active backup storage is <72 hours once the expedited job runs, but complete removal from archival cold-tier could take up to 30 days depending on provider immutability windows.
- Notification: we'll provide timestamped purge logs and the erase_evidence_matrix entries.

I recommend the contract commit read: live purge within 7 days; expedited backup purge propagation within 3 days; certification of full archival purge within 30 days, with an explicit carveout path for legally required archival retention (we'll record any such carveouts as Schedule exceptions).

Marcus
Head of Infra Ops, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@finovahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA redline: geolock and backup erasure window

Adding one operational note on BYOK/Private deployments: if Finova is concerned about cross-border backup controls, Dedicated or Private deployment options allow us to guarantee no cross-border copies are produced by isolating the tenant to an EU-only cluster and using customer-managed keys. That removes the need for a DR replication carveout in most cases.

If Finova wants to keep Hosted but tighten language, we can add the explicit notice-and-approval step for any region outside the enumerated EU list.

Also: we can include an SLA credit trigger if an expedited purge job misses the stated propagation window; Laura — do you want us to include capped credits or a remediation process only?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@finovahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA redline: geolock and backup erasure window

Olivia — thanks for the callouts and for reviewing our redline. After discussing with Product and Infra we can accept the following contract language today:

- Operational Regions: backups will only be replicated to the EU regions listed in Schedule 2. Any region outside that list requires Finova's prior written approval.
- Erasure commitment: live purge within 7 days; expedited backup purge propagation within 3 days of the expedited request; full archival purge certification within 30 days except for any lawful archival carveouts documented in Schedule exceptions.
- Evidence: Redwood to deliver the erase_evidence_matrix for each purge event and a timestamped purge log.
- SLA remediation: if Redwood misses the expedited purge propagation window, we will provide a defined remediation plan and a capped credit (not to exceed 1 month of service fees) as the agreed remedy.

Please see the attached redline (redwood_dpa_proposed_redline.docx) for the exact wording. If this matches Finova's needs we can issue a DocuSign envelope today.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_proposed_redline.docx
